Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verse 9–15:

{9-10} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), in the form of a rhetorical question that emphasizes and magnifies this story: {Has the story of Musa reached you?} In his state, which was the beginning of his happiness and the source of his prophethood: that he saw a fire from afar, for he had lost his way, the cold had afflicted him, and he had nothing with which to warm himself on his journey. So he said to his family: {Indeed, I have perceived a fire} — i.e., I saw {a fire}, and that was on the side of the Tur, the right-hand side. {Perhaps I can bring you from it a burning brand} — by which you may warm yourselves — {or find at the fire guidance} — i.e., someone who will guide me to the way. His aim was physical light and physical guidance, but he found there spiritual light: the light of revelation by which spirits and hearts are illuminated, and true guidance: the guidance to the straight path that leads to the Gardens of Bliss. Thus there befell him a matter that was not in his calculation and had not crossed his mind.

{11} {Then when he came to it} — i.e., the fire he had perceived from afar, which in reality was light, and it is a fire that burns and also illuminates. This is shown by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "His veil is light, or fire; were He to lift it, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever His sight reached." When he arrived at it, he was called from it — i.e., Allah called him, as He said: {And We called him from the right side of the mount and brought him near in confidence}.

{12} {Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.} He informed him that He is his Lord, and commanded him to prepare and make ready for His intimate address, and to take it seriously, and to cast off his sandals, because he was in the sacred, purified, and exalted valley. Even if its sanctity were only that He chose it for His address to His interlocutor Musa, that would suffice. Many commentators have said that Allah commanded him to remove his sandals because they were made of donkey hide; but Allah knows best.

{13} {And I have chosen you} — i.e., I selected you and chose you from among the people. This is the greatest blessing and favor that Allah bestowed upon him, and it requires of him the gratitude that befits it. For this reason He said: {So listen to what is revealed} — i.e., give ear to what has been revealed to you, for it deserves that, since it is the foundation and origin of the religion and the pillar of the Islamic call.

{14} Then He explained what He reveals to him, saying: {Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me} — i.e., Allah, who alone deserves divinity and is characterized by it, because He is perfect in His names and attributes, singular in His actions, having no partner, no equal, no peer, and no namesake. {So worship Me} — in all kinds of worship, outward and inward, its roots and branches. Then He singled out prayer for mention, although it is included in worship, because of its excellence, nobility, and its embodying the servitude of the heart, tongue, and limbs. His saying {for My remembrance} — the lam is causal: i.e., establish prayer for the sake of remembering Me, because the remembrance of Allah the Exalted is the noblest of aims, through it comes the servitude of the heart, and through it comes happiness. A heart idle from the remembrance of Allah is idle from every good and is utterly ruined. So Allah prescribed for the servants various kinds of worship whose purpose is establishing His remembrance, especially prayer. Allah the Exalted said: {Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing; and the remembrance of Allah is greater} — i.e., the remembrance of Allah within it is greater than its prohibition of immorality and wrongdoing. This type is called the Tawhid of Divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah) and the Tawhid of worship (tawhid al-ibadah): divinity is an attribute of Allah the Exalted, and servitude is the attribute of His servant.

{15} {Indeed, the Hour is coming} — i.e., its occurrence is unavoidable. {I am about to conceal it} — i.e., from myself, as in some readings; like His saying: {They ask you about the Hour: say, its knowledge is only with Allah}, and He said: {With Him is the knowledge of the Hour}. Its knowledge He has concealed from all creation; no angel brought near nor prophet sent knows it. The wisdom in the coming of the Hour is {that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives} — good or evil; so it is the gateway to the abode of recompense: {that He may reward those who did evil according to what they did and reward those who did good with the best}.

{9-10} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), in the form of a rhetorical question that emphasizes and magnifies this story: {Has the story of Musa reached you?} In his state, which was the beginning of his happiness and the source of his prophethood: that he saw a fire from afar, for he had lost his way, the cold had afflicted him, and he had nothing with which to warm himself on his journey. So he said to his family: {Indeed, I have perceived a fire} — i.e., I saw {a fire}, and that was on the side of the Tur, the right-hand side. {Perhaps I can bring you from it a burning brand} — by which you may warm yourselves — {or find at the fire guidance} — i.e., someone who will guide me to the way. His aim was physical light and physical guidance, but he found there spiritual light: the light of revelation by which spirits and hearts are illuminated, and true guidance: the guidance to the straight path that leads to the Gardens of Bliss. Thus there befell him a matter that was not in his calculation and had not crossed his mind.

{11} {Then when he came to it} — i.e., the fire he had perceived from afar, which in reality was light, and it is a fire that burns and also illuminates. This is shown by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "His veil is light, or fire; were He to lift it, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever His sight reached." When he arrived at it, he was called from it — i.e., Allah called him, as He said: {And We called him from the right side of the mount and brought him near in confidence}.

{12} {Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.} He informed him that He is his Lord, and commanded him to prepare and make ready for His intimate address, and to take it seriously, and to cast off his sandals, because he was in the sacred, purified, and exalted valley. Even if its sanctity were only that He chose it for His address to His interlocutor Musa, that would suffice. Many commentators have said that Allah commanded him to remove his sandals because they were made of donkey hide; but Allah knows best.

{13} {And I have chosen you} — i.e., I selected you and chose you from among the people. This is the greatest blessing and favor that Allah bestowed upon him, and it requires of him the gratitude that befits it. For this reason He said: {So listen to what is revealed} — i.e., give ear to what has been revealed to you, for it deserves that, since it is the foundation and origin of the religion and the pillar of the Islamic call.

{14} Then He explained what He reveals to him, saying: {Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me} — i.e., Allah, who alone deserves divinity and is characterized by it, because He is perfect in His names and attributes, singular in His actions, having no partner, no equal, no peer, and no namesake. {So worship Me} — in all kinds of worship, outward and inward, its roots and branches. Then He singled out prayer for mention, although it is included in worship, because of its excellence, nobility, and its embodying the servitude of the heart, tongue, and limbs. His saying {for My remembrance} — the lam is causal: i.e., establish prayer for the sake of remembering Me, because the remembrance of Allah the Exalted is the noblest of aims, through it comes the servitude of the heart, and through it comes happiness. A heart idle from the remembrance of Allah is idle from every good and is utterly ruined. So Allah prescribed for the servants various kinds of worship whose purpose is establishing His remembrance, especially prayer. Allah the Exalted said: {Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing; and the remembrance of Allah is greater} — i.e., the remembrance of Allah within it is greater than its prohibition of immorality and wrongdoing. This type is called the Tawhid of Divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah) and the Tawhid of worship (tawhid al-ibadah): divinity is an attribute of Allah the Exalted, and servitude is the attribute of His servant.

{15} {Indeed, the Hour is coming} — i.e., its occurrence is unavoidable. {I am about to conceal it} — i.e., from myself, as in some readings; like His saying: {They ask you about the Hour: say, its knowledge is only with Allah}, and He said: {With Him is the knowledge of the Hour}. Its knowledge He has concealed from all creation; no angel brought near nor prophet sent knows it. {16} That is: let not be an obstacle to you, nor let distract you from belief in the Hour, the recompense, and working for it, the one who disbelieves in it, not holding to its occurrence, who strives to cast doubt upon it and to sow doubt about it, disputes concerning it with falsehood, and presents such dubious arguments as he is able; following in this his own desire, his aim not being to reach the truth, but his utmost goal being to follow his desire. So beware of listening to one whose state is this, or accepting any of his sayings and deeds that turn people away from belief in it and from striving for it as it deserves. Allah the Exalted only warned against one in this state because he is among the greatest dangers to the believer through his whisperings and deception, and because souls are naturally inclined to imitate and emulate their fellow kind. In this is a reminder and an indication of warning against every caller to falsehood who turns people away from obligatory faith or from its perfection, or who casts doubt into the heart, and against looking into books that contain such things.

He mentioned here belief in Him, worshipping Him, and belief in the Last Day, because these three matters are the foundations of faith and the pillar of religion. When they are complete, the matter of religion is complete, and it is diminished or lost by the diminishing or loss of any of them. This is similar to His saying, the Exalted, in reporting the measure of happiness and misery of the sects who were given the Book:
﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians — whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds — no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ And His saying: ﴿and thus perish﴾; that is: perish and be wretched if you follow the path of one who turns people away from it. And His saying, the Exalted:

{17} When God had explained to Musa the foundation of faith, He wished to show him some of His signs, by which his heart would be reassured, his eye comforted, and his faith strengthened through God's support against his enemy. So He said: {And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?} This was asked while God already knew; but to increase attention to this matter, the speech was delivered in the form of a question.

{18} Musa said: {It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep} (2). He mentioned in it these two benefits: a benefit for the human species, which is that he leans on it in standing and walking; and a benefit and help for the animals, which is that he would graze the sheep, and when he grazed them among the khabt trees and the like, he would beat them down (hashsha), that is, strike the trees so that their leaves fall and the sheep can eat them. This good character of Musa, peace be upon him, whose effects include the good care of dumb animals and kindness towards them, indicates a care from God for him, a choosing and a distinction that is required by God's mercy and wisdom. {And I have in it other uses (ma'arib)}, that is, purposes other than these two matters.

Among the courtesy of Musa, peace be upon him, is that when God asked him about what was in his right hand, and the question could be understood as asking about its substance or its use, he answered by describing both its substance and its use.

{19–20} God said to him: {Throw it down, O Musa.} So he threw it down, and behold, it was a serpent gliding (tas'a). It was transformed, by God's permission, into a great serpent. Musa fled in fear and did not turn back.

Describing it as "gliding" removes a possible suspicion, namely that one might think it was an illusion and not a reality; its gliding removes this doubt.

{21} God said to Musa: {Take hold of it and do not fear}; that is, there is no harm to you from it. {We shall return it to its former state}; that is, its form and characteristics, since it had been a staff. So Musa obeyed God's command, out of faith in Him and submission, and took it, and his staff returned to what he used to know. This is one sign.

{22} Then He mentioned the other sign, saying: {And draw your hand to your side (junah)}; that is, put your hand into your pocket (jayb), and press your upper arm (adud) to yourself, which is the wing (junah) of a person; {it will come out white, without harm}; that is, a radiant whiteness without defect or leprosy. {As another sign.}

{23} God said: {These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs; indeed they are a people who are defiantly disobedient.} {That We may show you of Our greatest signs}; that is, We did what We mentioned of the staff's transformation into a gliding serpent and of the hand coming out white for those who look, in order that We may show you of Our greatest signs, which indicate the truth of your message and the reality of what you brought, so that your heart may be reassured, your knowledge increased, and you may trust God's promise to you of protection and victory, and so that you may be a proof and a demonstration to those to whom you are sent.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verses 42–46:

{42} When Allah had bestowed upon Musa the favours, both religious and worldly, with which He had favoured him, He said to him: {Go, you and your brother} — Harun — {with My signs}; that is, the signs from Me, which indicate the truth and its beauty and the ugliness of falsehood, such as the hand and the staff and the like, {in nine signs, to Pharaoh and his chiefs}. {And do not slacken in remembering Me}; that is, do not falter or grow lax in continually remembering Me, persisting in it and holding fast to it as you were promised, {so that We may glorify You much and remember You much}. Indeed, the remembrance of Allah is a help in all matters: it makes them easy and lightens their burden.

{43} {Go to Pharaoh; indeed he has transgressed}; that is, he has exceeded the limit in his disbelief, his tyranny, his wrongdoing and his aggression.

{44} {Speak to him a gentle word}; that is, a word that is easy and kind, spoken with gentleness, softness and courtesy in speech, without indecency, arrogance or harshness in utterance or roughness in conduct. {Perhaps he will be reminded}: by means of the gentle word, {of what will benefit him, and so come to it, {or fear}: what will harm him, and so abandon it}; for a gentle word calls to that, while a harsh word repels its hearer. The gentle word is explained in His saying: {So say, "Would you like to purify yourself? And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear Him"}. In this speech there is so much gentleness and ease, and such freedom from harshness, as is not hidden from the reflective. For he began with {would you like} (hal), which indicates offering and consultation, a thing from which no one recoils; and he invited him to purify himself and cleanse himself of impurities, the root of which is purification from polytheism, which every sound mind accepts. He did not say, "I will purify you," but said {purify yourself}, by your own self. Then he called him to the way of his Lord, who had nurtured him and bestowed upon him outward and inward blessings, which deserve to be repaid with gratitude and remembrance, and he said: {And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear Him}. When he did not accept this gentle speech, which takes hold of hearts by its beauty, it was known that admonition would not benefit him, so Allah seized him with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

{45} {They said, "Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us}; that is, that he will rush upon us with punishment and attack us before You have conveyed Your messages to him and established the proof against him, {or that he will transgress}; that is, that he will rebel against the truth and act tyrannically through his kingdom, his authority, his army and his helpers.

{46} {He said, "Do not fear}: that he will hasten against you; {indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing"}; that is, you are under My protection and care; I hear your speech and I see all your circumstances, so do not fear him. Thus fear departed from them, and their hearts were reassured by the promise of their Lord.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verses 47–48:

{47} That is: they came to him with these two matters: calling him to Islam (submission to God), and freeing this noble people, the Children of Israel, from his bondage and enslavement of them, so that they might be liberated and take charge of their own affairs, and so that Moses might establish among them the Law and religion of God. {Indeed, we have come to you with a sign}: one that testifies to our truthfulness. Moses then threw down his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent; and he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the beholders... and so on, to the end of what God has related of the two of them. {And peace is upon those who follow the guidance}; that is, those who follow the straight path and are guided by the clear Law: for them there is safety in this world and the Hereafter.

{48} {Indeed, it has been revealed to us}; that is, our message comes from God, not from ourselves; {that the punishment is upon him who denies and turns away}; that is, who denies the reports of God and the reports of His messengers, and turns away from submitting to them and following them. This contains an encouragement to Pharaoh to believe, affirm, and follow them, and a warning against the opposite of that. But this admonition and reminder did not benefit him: he denied his Lord, disbelieved, and disputed about that out of wrongdoing and obstinacy.

{48} {Indeed, it has been revealed to us}; that is, our message comes from God, not from ourselves; {that the punishment is upon him who denies and turns away}; that is, who denies the reports of God and the reports of His messengers, and turns away from submitting to them and following them. This contains an encouragement to Pharaoh to believe, affirm, and follow them, and a warning against the opposite of that. But this admonition and reminder did not benefit him: he denied his Lord, disbelieved, and disputed about that out of wrongdoing and obstinacy.

{49} That is, Pharaoh said to Musa, in a manner of denial: ﴿Who then is the Lord of you both, O Musa?﴾

{50} Musa answered with a reply that is sufficient, clear, and conclusive, saying: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its form and then guided it.﴾ That is, our Lord is the One who created all creatures and gave each creature the form suited to it, [indicating] the excellence of the workmanship of what He created, in its size, smallness, moderation, and all its attributes. Then He guided every creature to that for which He created it. This complete guidance is observed in all creatures. You find every creature striving for the benefits for which it was created and for the repelling of harm from itself. Indeed, God gave the animals such intellect as enables them to do so. This is like His saying: ﴿Who made good everything He created﴾. So the One who created the creatures, gave them their good form which the intellects cannot propose anything better than, and guided them to their interests, is the Lord in truth. Denying Him is therefore a denial of the greatest of existing things, a stubborn obstinacy and an open lie. Even if it were supposed that a human denied any of the known matters that he denied, his denial of the Lord of the worlds would be greater than that.

{51} For this reason, when Pharaoh could not contend against this decisive proof, he turned to confusion, deviated from the point, and said to Musa: ﴿What then is the state of the former generations?﴾ That is, what is their condition, and what is their news? How did they come to their state, when they preceded us in denial, disbelief, wrongdoing, and obstinacy, and we have them as an example?

{52} Musa said: ﴿Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.﴾ That is, He has counted their deeds, good and bad, and recorded them in His Book, which is the Preserved Tablet, and He encompasses them with knowledge and information. So He does not stray from any of them, and He does not forget what He has known of them. The meaning of this is that they have come before what they had sent forward, and they will meet their deeds and be recompensed for them. So there is no point in your question and inquiry about them, O Pharaoh: ﴿That is a community that has passed away; for them is what they earned, and for you is what you earn.﴾ If the proof we presented to you and the signs we showed you have been verified by you as true and certain, and this is the reality, then submit to the truth, leave off disbelief, wrongdoing, and much disputation with falsehood. If you have doubted them, or seen them as not upright, then the way is open and the door of inquiry is not closed. So refute the proof with a proof and the demonstration with a demonstration, and you will not find a way to that as long as the two changes (night and day) endure. How, when God has reported about him that he denied them while his soul was certain of them, as He said: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾? And Musa said: ﴿You certainly know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear evidences﴾? Thus it is known that he was a wrongdoer in his disputation, whose aim was arrogance in the land.

{53} Then he (Musa) continued on this decisive proof by mentioning many of His blessings and His necessary kindness, saying: ﴿He who made the earth for you a cradle﴾. That is, a bed in a state in which you are able to settle in it, to rest, to build, to plant, and to till it for sowing and other purposes. He made it submissive for that, and did not make it refuse any of your interests. ﴿And threaded for you therein roads﴾. That is, He made passable for you the routes that connect one land to another and one region to another, so that human beings are able to reach all parts of the earth in the easiest manner, and benefit from their journeys more than from their residence. ﴿And sent down from the sky water, and We brought forth thereby pairs of various plants﴾. That is, He sent down rain, and by it revived the earth after its death, and caused to grow all kinds of plants with their different types, varied forms, and differing conditions. He drove it, decreed it, and facilitated it as provision for us and for our livestock. Had it not been for that, whoever is upon it, of humans and animals, would have perished.

{54} For this reason He said: ﴿Eat, and pasture your livestock﴾. Its context is in the manner of favour, to indicate that the original ruling regarding all plants is permissibility. So nothing of them is forbidden except what is harmful, such as poisons and the like. ﴿Surely in that are signs for people of sound intellect﴾. That is, for those with steady minds and upright thoughts, [to see the signs] of God's grace, His kindness, His mercy, the vastness of His generosity, and the completeness of His care; and [to see] that He is the Lord, the worshipped, the Owner, the Praiseworthy, who alone deserves worship, and that praise, commendation, and thanks belong only to the one who bestowed these blessings; and [to see] that He is over all things Powerful. Just as He revived the earth after its death, so surely He is the One who gives life to the dead. As for others, they are like grazing beasts and pasturing livestock. They do not look at it with the gaze of reflection, and their insight does not penetrate to its purpose. Rather, their share is the share of beasts: they eat and drink while their hearts are heedless and their bodies are turned away. ﴿And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth that they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾.

{55} Having mentioned the generosity of the earth and its good response to what God sends down upon it of rain, and that by the permission of its Lord it brings forth plants of differing kinds, He informed that He created us from it, and in it He will return us when we die and are buried in it, and from it He will bring us forth ﴿once again﴾. Just as He brought us into existence from it out of nothing, and we know this and are certain of it, so He will return us by resurrection from it after our death, in order to recompense us for the deeds we performed upon it. These are two clear rational proofs of the return: the bringing forth of plants from the earth after its death, and the bringing forth of the responsible beings from it at their creation.

{49} That is, Pharaoh said to Musa, in a manner of denial: ﴿Who then is the Lord of you both, O Musa?﴾

{50} Musa answered with a reply that is sufficient, clear, and conclusive, saying: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its form and then guided it.﴾ That is, our Lord is the One who created all creatures and gave each creature the form suited to it, [indicating] the excellence of the workmanship of what He created, in its size, smallness, moderation, and all its attributes. Then He guided every creature to that for which He created it. This complete guidance is observed in all creatures. You find every creature striving for the benefits for which it was created and for the repelling of harm from itself. Indeed, God gave the animals such intellect as enables them to do so. This is like His saying: ﴿Who made good everything He created﴾. So the One who created the creatures, gave them their good form which the intellects cannot propose anything better than, and guided them to their interests, is the Lord in truth. Denying Him is therefore a denial of the greatest of existing things, a stubborn obstinacy and an open lie. Even if it were supposed that a human denied any of the known matters that he denied, his denial of the Lord of the worlds would be greater than that.

{51} For this reason, when Pharaoh could not contend against this decisive proof, he turned to confusion, deviated from the point, and said to Musa: ﴿What then is the state of the former generations?﴾ That is, what is their condition, and what is their news? How did they come to their state, when they preceded us in denial, disbelief, wrongdoing, and obstinacy, and we have them as an example?

{52} Musa said: ﴿Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.﴾ That is, He has counted their deeds, good and bad, and recorded them in His Book, which is the Preserved Tablet, and He encompasses them with knowledge and information. So He does not stray from any of them, and He does not forget what He has known of them. The meaning of this is that they have come before what they had sent forward, and they will meet their deeds and be recompensed for them. So there is no point in your question and inquiry about them, O Pharaoh: ﴿That is a community that has passed away; for them is what they earned, and for you is what you earn.﴾ If the proof we presented to you and the signs we showed you have been verified by you as true and certain, and this is the reality, then submit to the truth, leave off disbelief, wrongdoing, and much disputation with falsehood. If you have doubted them, or seen them as not upright, then the way is open and the door of inquiry is not closed. So refute the proof with a proof and the demonstration with a demonstration, and you will not find a way to that as long as the two changes (night and day) endure. How, when God has reported about him that he denied them while his soul was certain of them, as He said: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾? And Musa said: ﴿You certainly know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear evidences﴾? Thus it is known that he was a wrongdoer in his disputation, whose aim was arrogance in the land.

{53} Then he (Musa) continued on this decisive proof by mentioning many of His blessings and His necessary kindness, saying: ﴿He who made the earth for you a cradle﴾. That is, a bed in a state in which you are able to settle in it, to rest, to build, to plant, and to till it for sowing and other purposes. He made it submissive for that, and did not make it refuse any of your interests. ﴿And threaded for you therein roads﴾. That is, He made passable for you the routes that connect one land to another and one region to another, so that human beings are able to reach all parts of the earth in the easiest manner, and benefit from their journeys more than from their residence. ﴿And sent down from the sky water, and We brought forth thereby pairs of various plants﴾. That is, He sent down rain, and by it revived the earth after its death, and caused to grow all kinds of plants with their different types, varied forms, and differing conditions. He drove it, decreed it, and facilitated it as provision for us and for our livestock. Had it not been for that, whoever is upon it, of humans and animals, would have perished.

{54} For this reason He said: ﴿Eat, and pasture your livestock﴾. Its context is in the manner of favour, to indicate that the original ruling regarding all plants is permissibility. So nothing of them is forbidden except what is harmful, such as poisons and the like. ﴿Surely in that are signs for people of sound intellect﴾. That is, for those with steady minds and upright thoughts, [to see the signs] of God's grace, His kindness, His mercy, the vastness of His generosity, and the completeness of His care; and [to see] that He is the Lord, the worshipped, the Owner, the Praiseworthy, who alone deserves worship, and that praise, commendation, and thanks belong only to the one who bestowed these blessings; and [to see] that He is over all things Powerful. Just as He revived the earth after its death, so surely He is the One who gives life to the dead. God specified those of sound intellect for this because they are the ones who benefit from it, and who look at it with the gaze of reflection. As for others, they are like grazing beasts and pasturing livestock. They do not look at it with the gaze of reflection, and their insight does not penetrate to its purpose. Rather, their share is the share of beasts: they eat and drink while their hearts are heedless and their bodies are turned away. ﴿And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth that they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾.

{55} Having mentioned the generosity of the earth and its good response to what God sends down upon it of rain, and that by the permission of its Lord it brings forth plants of differing kinds, He informed that He created us from it, and in it He will return us when we die and are buried in it, and from it He will bring us forth ﴿once again﴾. {56} Allah, exalted is He, informs that He showed Pharaoh all the signs, proofs and decisive evidences of every kind: the visible (ʿiyaniyyah), the horizontal (afaqiyyah) and the internal (nafsiyyah). Yet he did not become upright nor did he refrain; rather, he denied and turned away. He denied the report and turned away from the command and prohibition, made truth into falsehood and falsehood into truth, and disputed with falsehood in order to lead the people astray.

{57} He said: ﴿Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic?﴾ He claimed that these signs which Moses showed him were sorcery and deception, whose purpose was to expel them from their land and seize it, so that his speech would have an effect on the hearts of his people, for natures incline towards their homelands and find it hard to leave and part from them. Thus he informed them that this was Moses' intention, so that they would hate him and strive to fight him.

{58} ﴿So we will surely bring you magic like yours.﴾ ﴿So set between us a appointment, which we will not fail to keep, neither we nor you, at a place equitable (suwa)﴾: that is, a place level, known to us and to you, or an even, moderate place where we can be able to see what is in it.

{59} Moses said: ﴿Your appointment is the Day of Adornment﴾: it is their festival, in which they are free and set aside their preoccupations. ﴿And that the people be gathered in the forenoon﴾: that is, that they all be assembled at the time of forenoon (ḍuḥā). Moses requested this because on the Day of Adornment and at the forenoon of it there occurs a great gathering and seeing of things as they truly are, which does not occur at other times.

{60} ﴿So Pharaoh withdrew and gathered his scheming﴾: that is, all that he was able to devise to plot against Moses. He sent to his cities for those who would gather the skilled magicians in their magic, and sorcery was then widespread and its knowledge desired, so he gathered a great multitude of magicians. Then each of them came to the appointment, and the people assembled for the appointment, and the gathering was grand, attended by men and women, the nobles and the notables, the common folk, the young and the old. They urged the people to gather, saying ﴿to the people: Will you gather, that we may follow the magicians if they are the victors?﴾

{61} When they had assembled from all the regions, Moses, peace be upon him, admonished them and established the proof against them, saying to them: ﴿Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment﴾: that is, do not support what you are upon of falsehood with your sorcery, contending against the truth and inventing lies against Allah, for He will uproot you with a punishment from Him and frustrate your effort and your fabrication; you will not attain what you seek of victory and rank with Pharaoh and his chiefs, nor will you be safe from the punishment of Allah.

{62} The word of truth must certainly affect hearts. Indeed, the dispute and contention among the magicians ceased when they heard Moses' words and became confused, and perhaps part of their dispute was doubt about Moses: is he upon the truth or not? But their affair was not yet settled, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was already decreed, that whoever perished might perish upon clear proof and whoever lived might live upon clear proof. Then they secretly conferred among themselves, agreeing upon one statement, so that their speech and action would succeed and the people would hold to their religion.

{63} The secret conference they held Allah explained by His saying: ﴿They said: Indeed these two are certainly magicians who wish to drive you out of your land with their magic﴾, like the previous statement of Pharaoh. Either this was agreement between Pharaoh and the magicians on this statement without intention, or it was Pharaoh's instruction to them of the statement he had resolved upon and displayed to the people. They added to Pharaoh's words, saying: ﴿and they will take away your most excellent way﴾: that is, the way of magic, which they envy you for, and he wishes to prevail over you so that he may have the glory, fame and renown, and he himself would be the aim of this knowledge with which you have occupied your time, and what you used to earn your livelihood by would be lost to you, along with what follows from it of leadership.

{64} This was an incitement by some of them against others to strive in opposing him. For this reason they said: ﴿So gather your scheming﴾: that is, bring it forth all at once, united, supporting one another, helping one another, your opinion and word in agreement, ﴿then come in a row﴾: so that it would be more effective for your action and more awe-inspiring to hearts, and so that none of you would leave any part of what he is able to do. ﴿And know that whoever prevails today and succeeds and overcomes others, he is the one who prospers and wins.﴾ This is a day that will be followed by other days. How firm they were in their falsehood and how intense in it! They brought every means, instrument, possibility and stratagem by which they plotted against the truth.

{65} Allah refuses except to perfect His light and make the truth prevail over falsehood. When their stratagem was complete and their intention was focused, and nothing remained but action, ﴿they said﴾ to Moses: ﴿Either you throw, or we will be the first to throw.﴾ They gave him the choice, showing that they were certain of prevailing over him in any case.

{66} Moses said to them: ﴿Rather, you throw.﴾ So they threw their ropes and staffs; ﴿and behold, their ropes and staffs appeared to him, by their magic, to be moving﴾: that is, to Moses, ﴿that they were slithering﴾: [that they were snakes slithering].

{67} When that appeared to Moses, he sensed fear within himself, as is the demand of human nature; otherwise, he was certain of Allah's promise and victory.

{68} ﴿We said to him﴾ as firm assurance and reassurance: ﴿Do not fear; indeed you are the superior﴾ over them: that is, you will prevail over them, subdue them, and they will be humbled before you and submit.

{69} ﴿And throw what is in your right hand﴾: that is, your staff; ﴿it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only the trickery of a magician, and a magician does not succeed wherever he comes﴾: that is, their scheme and deceit will bring them no fruit and no success, for it is of the schemes of magicians who deceive people, confuse falsehood and make it appear that they are upon the truth.

{70} Moses threw his staff, and it swallowed all that they had made and devoured it, while the people looked at that happening. The magicians knew with certain knowledge that this was not magic and that it was from Allah, so they hastened to faith, ﴿and the magicians were thrown down, prostrating﴾, saying: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.﴾ The truth thus came to pass, became manifest and shone forth, and magic, deceit and scheming were nullified in that great assembly; it became a clear proof and a mercy for the believers and a proof against the obstinate.

{71} Pharaoh said to the magicians: ﴿You have believed in him before I gave you permission﴾: that is, how did you dare to believe without consulting me or seeking my permission? He marvelled at this from them because of their courtesy towards him, their humility and their submission to him in every matter, and he made this one of those. Then Pharaoh persisted in his disbelief and transgression after this proof, made light of his people's judgment, and showed them that this victory of Moses over the magicians was not because the one with him possessed the truth, but because he and the magicians had colluded, plotted and devised to expel Pharaoh and his people from their lands; so his people accepted this deception from him and took it as true. ﴿So he made his people foolish, and they obeyed him; indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ Moreover, this statement he made does not enter the mind of anyone who has even a little sense and knowledge of reality. Moses came from Madyan alone, and when he came he did not gather with any of the magicians or others; rather, he hastened to call Pharaoh and his people and showed them the signs. Pharaoh wished to oppose what Moses had brought, so he strove as much as he could, sent to his cities for every knowledgeable sorcerer, and they came to him, and he promised them reward and rank if they prevailed. They strove to the utmost and schemed with the greatest scheming to overcome Moses, and what happened happened. Is it possible, or conceivable, in view of this, that they and Moses had plotted together and agreed on what occurred? This is among the most absurd impossibilities. Then Pharaoh threatened the magicians, saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides﴾, as is done to the warrior who strives for corruption: he cuts off his right hand and left foot. ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾: that is, in order that you be disgraced and humiliated. ﴿And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting﴾: meaning, by his claim, that he and his nation are more severe in punishment than Allah and more lasting, inverting realities and terrorizing those who have no intellect.

{72} For this reason, when the magicians recognized the truth, and Allah granted them the intellect by which they perceive realities, they answered him with their words: ﴿We will not prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs﴾ [that is, we will not choose you and what you promised us of reward and nearness over what Allah has shown us of clear signs], which indicate that Allah alone is the Lord and the Object of worship, alone exalted and honoured, and that whatever is other than Him is falsehood; ﴿and over Him who originated us and created us﴾, this will not happen. ﴿So decide what you will decide﴾: of what you have threatened us with, of cutting, crucifixion and punishment. ﴿You only decide for this worldly life﴾: that is, what you threaten us with is at most what can occur in this worldly life, which ends and passes away and cannot harm us, unlike the punishment of Allah for whoever persists in his disbelief, which is lasting and great. This was as if it were their answer to his saying: ﴿And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.﴾ In this statement of the magicians is evidence that a sensible person ought to weigh the pleasures of this world against the pleasures of the Hereafter, and the punishment of this world against the punishment of the Hereafter.

{73} ﴿Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins﴾: that is, our disbelief and disobedience, for faith expiates misdeeds, and repentance erases what came before it. Their saying ﴿and what you compelled us to of magic﴾, with which we opposed the truth, is evidence that they were not free in their earlier action, and that Pharaoh compelled them by force. Apparently, and Allah knows best, when Moses admonished them, as mentioned in His saying: ﴿Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment﴾, it affected them and had a great effect upon them, and for this reason they disputed after this speech and admonition. Perhaps this subtle point that settled in their hearts, their dislike of opposing truth with falsehood, and their doing what they did under duress, is what affected them, and Allah had mercy on them because of it, and granted them success in faith and repentance. ﴿And Allah is better﴾ than what you promised us of reward, rank and standing, ﴿and more lasting﴾ in reward and benevolence, not as Pharaoh said: ﴿And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting﴾; he means that he is more severe in punishment and more lasting.

Among all that came of the story of Moses with Pharaoh, Allah mentions that when He reaches the story of the magicians, Pharaoh threatened them with cutting and crucifixion, but He does not mention that he actually did that, and no sound hadith has come regarding it, and affirming that it occurred or did not occur depends on evidence. Allah knows best about that and other matters. [But his threatening them with that while he had power is evidence that it occurred, and because if it had not occurred Allah would have mentioned it, and because the transmitters agree upon it.]

They urged the people to gather, saying ﴿to the people: Will you gather, that we may follow the magicians if they are the victors?﴾

{62} The word of truth must certainly affect hearts. Indeed, the dispute and contention among the magicians ceased when they heard Moses' words and became confused, and perhaps part of their dispute was doubt about Moses: is he upon the truth or not? Then they secretly conferred among themselves, agreeing upon one statement, so that their speech and action would succeed and the people would hold to their religion.

{64} This was an incitement by some of them against others to strive in opposing him. {67} When that appeared to Moses, he sensed fear within himself, as is the demand of human nature; otherwise, he was certain of Allah's promise and victory.

The magicians knew with certain knowledge that this was not magic and that it was from Allah, so they hastened to faith, ﴿and the magicians were thrown down, prostrating﴾, saying: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.﴾ The truth thus came to pass, became manifest and shone forth, and magic, deceit and scheming were nullified in that great assembly; it became a clear proof and a mercy for the believers and a proof against the obstinate.

He marvelled at this from them because of their courtesy towards him, their humility and their submission to him in every matter, and he made this one of those. Then Pharaoh persisted in his disbelief and transgression after this proof, made light of his people's judgment, and showed them that this victory of Moses over the magicians was not because the one with him possessed the truth, but because he and the magicians had colluded, plotted and devised to expel Pharaoh and his people from their lands; so his people accepted this deception from him and took it as true. ﴿So he made his people foolish, and they obeyed him; indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ Moreover, this statement he made does not enter the mind of anyone who has even a little sense and knowledge of reality. {60} ﴿So Pharaoh withdrew and gathered his scheming﴾: that is, all that he was able to devise to plot against Moses. He sent to his cities for those who would gather the skilled magicians in their magic, and sorcery was then widespread and its knowledge desired, so he gathered a great multitude of magicians. Then each of them came to the appointment, and the people assembled for the appointment, and the gathering was grand, attended by men and women, the nobles and the notables, the common folk, the young and the old. They urged the people to gather, saying ﴿to the people: Will you gather, that we may follow the magicians if they are the victors?﴾

{61} When they had assembled from all the regions, Moses, peace be upon him, admonished them and established the proof against them, saying to them: ﴿Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment﴾: that is, do not support what you are upon of falsehood with your sorcery, contending against the truth and inventing lies against Allah, for He will uproot you with a punishment from Him and frustrate your effort and your fabrication; you will not attain what you seek of victory and rank with Pharaoh and his chiefs, nor will you be safe from the punishment of Allah.

{62} The word of truth must certainly affect hearts. Indeed, the dispute and contention among the magicians ceased when they heard Moses' words and became confused, and perhaps part of their dispute was doubt about Moses: is he upon the truth or not? But their affair was not yet settled, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was already decreed, that whoever perished might perish upon clear proof and whoever lived might live upon clear proof. Then they secretly conferred among themselves, agreeing upon one statement, so that their speech and action would succeed and the people would hold to their religion.

{63} The secret conference they held Allah explained by His saying: ﴿They said: Indeed these two are certainly magicians who wish to drive you out of your land with their magic﴾, like the previous statement of Pharaoh. Either this was agreement between Pharaoh and the magicians on this statement without intention, or it was Pharaoh's instruction to them of the statement he had resolved upon and displayed to the people. They added to Pharaoh's words, saying: ﴿and they will take away your most excellent way﴾: that is, the way of magic, which they envy you for, and he wishes to prevail over you so that he may have the glory, fame and renown, and he himself would be the aim of this knowledge with which you have occupied your time, and what you used to earn your livelihood by would be lost to you, along with what follows from it of leadership.

{64} This was an incitement by some of them against others to strive in opposing him. For this reason they said: ﴿So gather your scheming﴾: that is, bring it forth all at once, united, supporting one another, helping one another, your opinion and word in agreement, ﴿then come in a row﴾: so that it would be more effective for your action and more awe-inspiring to hearts, and so that none of you would leave any part of what he is able to do. ﴿And know that whoever prevails today and succeeds and overcomes others, he is the one who prospers and wins.﴾ This is a day that will be followed by other days. How firm they were in their falsehood and how intense in it! They brought every means, instrument, possibility and stratagem by which they plotted against the truth.

{65} Allah refuses except to perfect His light and make the truth prevail over falsehood. When their stratagem was complete and their intention was focused, and nothing remained but action, ﴿they said﴾ to Moses: ﴿Either you throw, or we will be the first to throw.﴾ They gave him the choice, showing that they were certain of prevailing over him in any case.

{66} Moses said to them: ﴿Rather, you throw.﴾ So they threw their ropes and staffs; ﴿and behold, their ropes and staffs appeared to him, by their magic, to be moving﴾: that is, to Moses, ﴿that they were slithering﴾: [that they were snakes slithering].

{67} When that appeared to Moses, he sensed fear within himself, as is the demand of human nature; otherwise, he was certain of Allah's promise and victory.

{68} ﴿We said to him﴾ as firm assurance and reassurance: ﴿Do not fear; indeed you are the superior﴾ over them: that is, you will prevail over them, subdue them, and they will be humbled before you and submit.

{69} ﴿And throw what is in your right hand﴾: that is, your staff; ﴿it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only the trickery of a magician, and a magician does not succeed wherever he comes﴾: that is, their scheme and deceit will bring them no fruit and no success, for it is of the schemes of magicians who deceive people, confuse falsehood and make it appear that they are upon the truth.

{70} Moses threw his staff, and it swallowed all that they had made and devoured it, while the people looked at that happening. The magicians knew with certain knowledge that this was not magic and that it was from Allah, so they hastened to faith, ﴿and the magicians were thrown down, prostrating﴾, saying: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.﴾ The truth thus came to pass, became manifest and shone forth, and magic, deceit and scheming were nullified in that great assembly; it became a clear proof and a mercy for the believers and a proof against the obstinate.

{71} Pharaoh said to the magicians: ﴿You have believed in him before I gave you permission﴾: that is, how did you dare to believe without consulting me or seeking my permission? He marvelled at this from them because of their courtesy towards him, their humility and their submission to him in every matter, and he made this one of those. Then Pharaoh persisted in his disbelief and transgression after this proof, made light of his people's judgment, and showed them that this victory of Moses over the magicians was not because the one with him possessed the truth, but because he and the magicians had colluded, plotted and devised to expel Pharaoh and his people from their lands; so his people accepted this deception from him and took it as true. ﴿So he made his people foolish, and they obeyed him; indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ Moreover, this statement he made does not enter the mind of anyone who has even a little sense and knowledge of reality. Moses came from Madyan alone, and when he came he did not gather with any of the magicians or others; rather, he hastened to call Pharaoh and his people and showed them the signs. Pharaoh wished to oppose what Moses had brought, so he strove as much as he could, sent to his cities for every knowledgeable sorcerer, and they came to him, and he promised them reward and rank if they prevailed. They strove to the utmost and schemed with the greatest scheming to overcome Moses, and what happened happened. Is it possible, or conceivable, in view of this, that they and Moses had plotted together and agreed on what occurred? This is among the most absurd impossibilities. Then Pharaoh threatened the magicians, saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides﴾, as is done to the warrior who strives for corruption: he cuts off his right hand and left foot. ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾: that is, in order that you be disgraced and humiliated. ﴿And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting﴾: meaning, by his claim, that he and his nation are more severe in punishment than Allah and more lasting, inverting realities and terrorizing those who have no intellect.

{72} For this reason, when the magicians recognized the truth, and Allah granted them the intellect by which they perceive realities, they answered him with their words: ﴿We will not prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs﴾ [that is, we will not choose you and what you promised us of reward and nearness over what Allah has shown us of clear signs], which indicate that Allah alone is the Lord and the Object of worship, alone exalted and honoured, and that whatever is other than Him is falsehood; ﴿and over Him who originated us and created us﴾, this will not happen. ﴿So decide what you will decide﴾: of what you have threatened us with, of cutting, crucifixion and punishment. ﴿You only decide for this worldly life﴾: that is, what you threaten us with is at most what can occur in this worldly life, which ends and passes away and cannot harm us, unlike the punishment of Allah for whoever persists in his disbelief, which is lasting and great. This was as if it were their answer to his saying: ﴿And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.﴾ In this statement of the magicians is evidence that a sensible person ought to weigh the pleasures of this world against the pleasures of the Hereafter, and the punishment of this world against the punishment of the Hereafter.

{73} ﴿Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins﴾: that is, our disbelief and disobedience, for faith expiates misdeeds, and repentance erases what came before it. Their saying ﴿and what you compelled us to of magic﴾, with which we opposed the truth, is evidence that they were not free in their earlier action, and that Pharaoh compelled them by force. Apparently, and Allah knows best, when Moses admonished them, as mentioned in His saying: ﴿Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment﴾, it affected them and had a great effect upon them, and for this reason they disputed after this speech and admonition. Then Pharaoh held them to account for that and compelled them to the scheme they had carried out, and for this reason they spoke with his previous statement before they came, saying: ﴿Indeed these two are certainly magicians who wish to drive you out of your land with their magic,﴾ so they proceeded according to what he had prescribed for them and compelled them to. Perhaps this subtle point that settled in their hearts, their dislike of opposing truth with falsehood, and their doing what they did under duress, is what affected them, and Allah had mercy on them because of it, and granted them success in faith and repentance. ﴿And Allah is better﴾ than what you promised us of reward, rank and standing, ﴿and more lasting﴾ in reward and benevolence, not as Pharaoh said: ﴿And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting﴾; he means that he is more severe in punishment and more lasting.

Among all that came of the story of Moses with Pharaoh, Allah mentions that when He reaches the story of the magicians, Pharaoh threatened them with cutting and crucifixion, but He does not mention that he actually did that, and no sound hadith has come regarding it, and affirming that it occurred or did not occur depends on evidence. Allah knows best about that and other matters. [But his threatening them with that while he had power is evidence that it occurred, and because if it had not occurred Allah would have mentioned it, and because the transmitters agree upon it.]

{74} God, exalted is He, informs that whoever comes to Him as a criminal (mujrim), meaning one characterized by sin in every respect, which necessarily entails disbelief, and persists in that state until he dies, then for him is the Fire of Hell, whose punishment is severe, whose shackles are great, whose depth is far-reaching, whose heat and cold are painful, in which is a punishment that melts livers and hearts. And from the intensity of that, the one tormented therein neither dies nor lives: he does not die so as to find rest, nor does he live a life in which he takes pleasure; rather his life is filled with torment of the heart, the spirit, and the body, which cannot be measured and is not relaxed for an hour. He calls for help and is not helped; he supplicates and is not answered. Indeed, when he seeks relief, he is given water like molten brass (al-muhl) that scorches the faces; and when he calls out, he is answered: ﴿Be silent therein, and do not speak to Me.﴾

{75–76} And whoever comes to his Lord as a believer in Him, affirming His messengers, following His books, and having done righteous deeds, both obligatory and recommended, ﴿for them are the high ranks﴾; that is, the lofty dwellings in decorated mansions, continuous pleasures, flowing rivers, eternal abiding, and great joy, in that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. And ﴿that﴾ reward is ﴿the recompense of one who purifies himself﴾; that is, who cleanses himself from polytheism, disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience, either by not committing them at all, or by repenting from what he has committed of them; and who also purifies his soul and causes it to grow through faith and righteous deeds. Indeed, purification (tazkiyah) has two meanings: cleansing and removing impurity, and increasing through the attainment of good; and zakah (alms) was named zakah for these two matters.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verses 77–79:

{77–79} When Musa had shown the proofs to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his people, he remained in Egypt calling them to Islam (submission to God) and striving to deliver the Children of Israel from Fir'awn and his torment, while Fir'awn persisted in arrogance and aversion, and his command was severe upon the Children of Israel. God showed him (Fir'awn) signs and lessons, which God has related to us in the Qur'an. The Children of Israel could not manifest and declare their faith; they had taken their houses as places of worship (masajid), and they endured Fir'awn and his harm. So God, may He be exalted, willed to rescue them from their enemy and to establish them in the land, so that they might worship Him openly and establish His command. He revealed to His prophet Musa that he should make an appointment with the Children of Israel in secret and that they should set out at the beginning of the night, so that they might go far into the land. He informed him that Fir'awn and his people would follow them. So they set out at the beginning of the night, all of the Children of Israel [and] their women and their offspring. When the people of Egypt awoke, they found that there was no one among them calling or responding. Their enemy Fir'awn was filled with rage against them, and he sent into the cities those who would gather people for him and urge them to go out in pursuit of the Children of Israel, [in order to attack them and vent his anger, while God is Overpowering over His affair; so Fir'awn's armies were complete, and he set out with them following the Children of Israel]. They followed them at sunrise. When the two groups came in sight of each other, the companions of Musa said: "Indeed, we are going to be overtaken!" and they were disturbed and afraid, for the sea was before them and Fir'awn was behind them, filled with rage and fury against them. But Musa's heart was at rest and his mind was calm, for he trusted in the promise of his Lord, and he said: {No indeed! Surely my Lord is with me; He will guide me.} So God revealed to him that he should strike the sea with his staff, and he struck it, and it parted into twelve paths, and the water became like lofty mountains on the right and left of the paths. God dried up their paths from which the water had parted, and God commanded them not to fear being overtaken by Fir'awn nor to dread drowning in the sea. So they walked along those paths. Fir'awn and his soldiers came and followed them along their route, until the people of Musa were all out and the people of Fir'awn were all in; God commanded the sea, and it closed over them, and there overcame them of the sea what overcame them, and they all drowned, and none of them was saved. The Children of Israel were watching their enemy, whose destruction God had made their eyes content with. This is the outcome of disbelief, misguidance, and failure to be guided by God's guidance. For this reason, He, may He be exalted, said: {And Fir'awn led his people astray}: by what he adorned for them of disbelief, and by his disparagement of what Musa brought and his belittling of them, and he never guided them at any time; so he brought them to the sources of error and misguidance, then brought them to the source of punishment and retribution.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 20, verses 80–82:**

{80–81} The Exalted reminds the Children of Israel of His great favor upon them in destroying their enemy, and of His appointment with Musa (peace be upon him) at the right side of the Mount (al-Tur), so that the Book containing the sublime rulings and beautiful reports might be revealed to him. Thus the religious blessing would be completed upon them after the worldly blessing. He also reminds them of His favor upon them in the wilderness (al-Tih, the desert of wandering) by sending down the manna and the quail, and the abundant, easily obtained provision that came to them without hardship. He said to them: ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you﴾; that is, give thanks to Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon you. ﴿And do not transgress therein﴾; that is, in His provision, by using it in disobedience to Him and by being insolent toward the blessing, for if you do that, ﴿My wrath will descend upon you﴾; that is, I will be angry with you and then punish you. ﴿And whoever has My wrath descend upon him has indeed perished﴾; that is, he has fallen, been destroyed, failed, and lost, because he has lost approval and goodness, and wrath and loss have descended upon him.

{82} Despite this, repentance is still offered, no matter what sins the servant has committed. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, I am Ever-Forgiving to he who repents﴾; that is, abundantly forgiving and merciful, ﴿from disbelief, innovation, and wickedness﴾, ﴿and believes﴾ in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, ﴿and does righteousness﴾ from the deeds of the heart, the body, and the tongue, ﴿and then remains steadfast upon guidance﴾; that is, he follows the straight path, adheres to the Noble Messenger, and follows the upright religion. For such a person, Allah forgives his burdens and pardons what preceded of his sin and persistence, because he has brought the greatest cause of forgiveness and mercy. Indeed, all causes are restricted to these matters: repentance erases what came before it, faith and Islam demolish what preceded them, and righteous deeds, which are good deeds, remove evil deeds. Following the paths of guidance in all their forms, such as learning knowledge, reflecting upon a verse or a hadith until a meaning becomes clear to him by which he is guided, calling people to the religion of truth, refuting an innovation, disbelief, or misguidance, striving (jihad), emigrating (hijrah), and other things, are all parts of guidance that expiate sins and attain the sought-after goal.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 20, verses 80–82:**

{80–81} The Exalted reminds the Children of Israel of His great favor upon them in destroying their enemy, and of His appointment with Musa (peace be upon him) at the right side of the Mount (al-Tur), so that the Book containing the sublime rulings and beautiful reports might be revealed to him. Thus the religious blessing would be completed upon them after the worldly blessing. He also reminds them of His favor upon them in the wilderness (al-Tih, the desert of wandering) by sending down the manna and the quail, and the abundant, easily obtained provision that came to them without hardship. He said to them: ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you﴾; that is, give thanks to Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon you. ﴿And do not transgress therein﴾; that is, in His provision, by using it in disobedience to Him and by being insolent toward the blessing, for if you do that, ﴿My wrath will descend upon you﴾; that is, I will be angry with you and then punish you. ﴿And whoever has My wrath descend upon him has indeed perished﴾; that is, he has fallen, been destroyed, failed, and lost, because he has lost approval and goodness, and wrath and loss have descended upon him.

{82} Despite this, repentance is still offered, no matter what sins the servant has committed. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, I am Ever-Forgiving to he who repents﴾; that is, abundantly forgiving and merciful, ﴿from disbelief, innovation, and wickedness﴾, ﴿and believes﴾ in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, ﴿and does righteousness﴾ from the deeds of the heart, the body, and the tongue, ﴿and then remains steadfast upon guidance﴾; that is, he follows the straight path, adheres to the Noble Messenger, and follows the upright religion. For such a person, Allah forgives his burdens and pardons what preceded of his sin and persistence, because he has brought the greatest cause of forgiveness and mercy. Indeed, all causes are restricted to these matters: repentance erases what came before it, faith and Islam demolish what preceded them, and righteous deeds, which are good deeds, remove evil deeds. Following the paths of guidance in all their forms, such as learning knowledge, reflecting upon a verse or a hadith until a meaning becomes clear to him by which he is guided, calling people to the religion of truth, refuting an innovation, disbelief, or misguidance, striving (jihad), emigrating (hijrah), and other things, are all parts of guidance that expiate sins and attain the sought-after goal.

{83} God Most High had promised Moses that he would come to Him so that He could send down the Torah to him, thirty nights, and He completed it with ten. When the appointed time was fulfilled, Moses, peace be upon him, hastened to attend the appointment, out of longing for his Lord and eagerness to meet His promise. God said to him: ﴿And what has made you hasten ahead of your people, O Moses?﴾; that is, what drove you ahead of them? And why did you not wait until you and they came together?

{84} ﴿He said: "They are right behind me."﴾; that is, close to me, and they will arrive following in my footsteps. "What hastened me to You, O my Lord, is the desire to draw near to You, to hasten toward Your pleasure, and to long for You."

{85} God said to him: ﴿Indeed, We have tested your people after you﴾; that is, by their worship of the calf, We tried and examined them, and they did not endure. When the trial reached them, they disbelieved. ﴿And al-Samiri misled them﴾: he brought out for them a calf, a body, which he had fashioned, and it had a lowing sound. He said to them: "This is your god and the god of Moses," but Moses had forgotten Him. So the Children of Israel were seduced by it and worshipped it. Harun (Aaron) forbade them, but they did not desist.

{86} When Moses returned to his people, ﴿angry and grieved﴾; that is, filled with rage, indignation and sorrow, he said to them, rebuking them and denouncing their deed: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾ This refers to the sending down of the Torah. ﴿Did the time seem long to you?﴾; that is, did the period seem long, so that you found my absence prolonged, when it was a short period? This is the view of many exegetes (tafsir: explanatory commentary on the Qur'an). It is also possible that the meaning is: did the era of prophethood and messengership seem long to you, so that you had no knowledge or trace of prophethood, its traces faded, and you had no news of it, so its marks were effaced through the long lapse of time, and you therefore worshipped other than God because ignorance prevailed and there was no knowledge of the traces of the message? That is, the matter is not so; rather, prophethood is among you, knowledge is established, and excuse is not accepted. ﴿Or did you desire﴾ by your action ﴿that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you﴾; that is, you exposed yourselves to its causes and rushed into what necessitates His punishment, and this is what has actually happened. ﴿So you broke your promise to me﴾, when I commanded you to be upright and entrusted you to Harun, but you neither observed the one who was absent nor honoured the one who was present.

{87–88} That is: they said to him, "We did not break our promise to you by our own choice or by our own will, but the thing that drove us to it is that we felt guilty about the ornaments of the people that we had with us." They had borrowed a great deal of jewelry from the Copts, as they recount, and they went out with it, and they threw it all into the fire and gathered it together when Musa (Moses) went away, intending to consult him about it when he returned. The Samiri (the Samaritan) had seen, on the day of the drowning, the trace of the Messenger, so his soul tempted him to take a handful from its trace, and that whatever he threw it upon would come alive, as a trial and a test. So he threw it upon that calf which he had fashioned in the form of a calf, and the calf moved and had a lowing and a voice. And they said, "Musa has gone off to seek his Lord, and he is here, but he has forgotten."

{89} This is from their dullness and the feebleness of their minds, for they saw this strange thing that had a lowing after having been an inanimate object, so they thought it to be the god of the earth and the heavens. "Do they not see that it does not return to them a word," that is, it does not speak, nor reply to them, nor do they reply to it, "nor does it possess for them any harm or any benefit?" So whoever lacks perfection, speech, and action does not deserve to be worshipped, and it is more deficient than its worshippers, for they speak and are able to bring about some benefits and the averting of some harms by God's empowering them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verses 90–94:

{90–91} That is: by their taking the calf [as a god], they are not excused in it. For although doubt had occurred to them regarding the origin of its worship, Harun had forbidden them from it, informed them that it was a trial (fitnah), and that their Lord is the Most Merciful (al-Rahman), from whom come the apparent and hidden blessings, the one who repels calamities, and that he commanded them to follow him and to withdraw from the calf. But they refused and said: ﴿We will not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾

{92–93} Then Musa turned to his brother, blaming him, and said: ﴿O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me?﴾ That is, [what prevented you from] informing me so that I might hasten back to them. ﴿Have you then disobeyed my order?﴾ That is, in my saying: ﴿Take my place among my people, act rightly, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.﴾ So Musa seized Harun by his head and his beard, dragging him out of anger and reproach toward him.

{94} Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother!﴾ This is a softening of [Musa's heart] toward him; otherwise he was his full brother. ﴿Do not seize my beard nor my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, "You have caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe my word."﴾ For you commanded me to take your place among them; had I followed you, I would have abandoned what you commanded me to uphold, I would have feared your censure, and you would say: "You have caused division among the Children of Israel," since you left them without a shepherd or a successor; this would divide them and scatter their unity. So do not make me among the wrongdoing people, and do not let the enemies rejoice over us. Then Musa regretted what he had done to his brother, though Harun did not deserve it, and said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy, and You are the most merciful of the merciful.﴾

Then he turned to the Samiri:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verse 95–97:

{95–96} That is: what is your affair, O Samiri, that you did what you did? He said: ﴿I saw what they did not see﴾, namely Jibril (peace be upon him) upon a horse, whom he saw at the time of their exit from the sea and the drowning of Pharaoh and his soldiers, according to what the commentators have said. ﴿So I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger's horse﴾, and I threw it upon the calf. ﴿And thus did my soul make it seem pleasing to me﴾: that I should take it and then throw it, and so it happened what happened.

{97} Then Musa said to him: ﴿Go﴾; that is, keep away from me and stay back from me. ﴿For you have in this life [the saying], "No contact"﴾; that is, you will be punished in this life with a punishment: no one will come near you and no one will touch you, so that whoever wishes to come close to you, you will say to him, "Do not touch me and do not come near me," as a punishment for that, since you touched what no one else touched and brought about what no one else brought about. ﴿And indeed for you is a promise you will not be failed in﴾: you will be recompensed for your deeds, of good and of evil. ﴿And look at your god to which you remained devoted﴾; that is, the calf. ﴿We will surely burn it and then scatter it into the sea, scattering﴾: Musa did that. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verses 99–101:

{99} Allah Most High bestows His favour upon His Prophet ﷺ by relating to him the news of earlier peoples and the reports of past generations, such as this great story and the rulings and other matters it contains, which none of the People of the Book deny. You did not study the accounts of the ancients, nor did you learn from anyone who had studied them. Therefore your reporting of these accounts with certain truth is evidence that you are truly the Messenger of Allah, and that what you have brought is true. For this reason He says: ﴿And We have certainly given you from Us a reminder﴾; that is, a precious gift and a generous bounty from Us. ﴿A reminder﴾ refers to this noble Qur'an: a reminder of the past and future reports, and a reminder through which one recalls the names and perfect attributes of Allah Most High, and through which one recalls the rulings of command and prohibition and the rulings of recompense. This indicates that the Qur'an contains the best of rulings, which sound minds and natural dispositions (fitrah) testify to their goodness and perfection, and the Qur'an reminds them of what Allah has placed within them. Since the Qur'an is a reminder for the Messenger and for his community, it is obligatory to receive it with acceptance, submission, compliance and veneration, to be guided by its light to the straight path, and to turn towards it with learning and teaching.

{100} As for turning away from it, or what is even greater than that, which is denial, it is ingratitude for this blessing, and whoever does so deserves punishment. For this reason He says: ﴿Whoever turns away from it﴾: by not believing in it, or by neglecting its commands and prohibitions, or its obligatory meanings to be learned. ﴿Indeed, he will carry on the Day of Resurrection a burden﴾: that is, his sin which caused him to turn away from the Qur'an and gave him over to disbelief and abandonment.

{101} ﴿Abiding therein﴾; that is, in their burden, because the punishment is the very deeds themselves, which turn into punishment for their doers according to their magnitude and smallness. ﴿And evil will it be for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load﴾; that is, how wretched is the load they carry and the punishment they suffer on the Day of Resurrection.
