His words ﴿On that Day intercession will not benefit, except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He approves﴾ mean: no one among the creatures will intercede with Him except one whom He has permitted to intercede, and He permits only one whose word, that is, whose intercession, He approves, from among the prophets, the messengers and His near servants, concerning those whose word and deed He approves, namely the sincere believer. If any of these conditions is lacking, there is no way for anyone to intercede for anyone.

{111–112} On that standing place people will be divided into two groups. The first are wrongdoers through their disbelief and evil; for them there is nothing but disappointment, deprivation, painful punishment in Hell, and the wrath of the Recompenser. The second group are those who believed in the manner commanded and did righteous deeds, both obligatory and recommended. ﴿They will not fear wrongdoing﴾; that is, an increase in their misdeeds, ﴿nor diminution﴾; that is, a reduction in their good deeds. Rather, their sins will be forgiven, their faults purified, and their good deeds multiplied, ﴿and if it is a good deed, He will double it and give from Himself a great reward﴾.

{113} That is: thus We have sent down this Book in a virtuous Arabic tongue, which you understand and comprehend, so that neither its wording nor its meaning is hidden from you. {And We have varied in it of the warning}; that is, We have diversified it into many kinds: at times by mentioning His names that indicate justice and retribution; at times by mentioning the exemplary punishments He inflicted upon earlier nations, which He commanded later nations to take heed from; at times by mentioning the effects of sins and the defects they earn; at times by mentioning the terrors of the Resurrection and the disturbing, frightening things within it; and at times by mentioning Hell and the various kinds of punishment and types of torment within it. All of this is out of mercy for the servants. {That they may fear Allah}, so that they abandon the evil and sins that harm them, {or it may cause them to remember}, so that they do the acts of obedience and good that benefit them. Thus, its being in Arabic and its being varied in its warnings are the greatest cause and the most important motive for piety and righteous action; had it been non-Arabic or not varied in its warnings, it would not have had this effect.

{114} When Allah the Exalted mentioned His judgment regarding His servants, both the judgment of recompense and the judgment of command in religion that He sent down in the Book, and this was among the effects of His dominion, He said:

﴿So exalted is Allah﴾, that is, He is majestic, lofty, and sanctified above every deficiency and defect. ﴿The King﴾, to whom sovereignty belongs as an attribute, while all creation are His subjects, and the judgments of His dominion, both decreed and legislated, take effect over them. ﴿The Truth﴾, that is, His existence, His dominion, and His perfection are true. Attributes of perfection are truly realized only in the One of majesty, and sovereignty is among them. As for other than Him among creatures, even if one has dominion at certain times over certain things, that dominion is limited and false, and it passes away. As for the Lord, He has never ceased and never will cease to be the living, self-subsisting, glorious King.

﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed﴾, that is, do not rush to seize the Qur'an while Jibril recites it to you, but be patient until he finishes. When he has finished, then recite it, for Allah has guaranteed to you its collection in your breast and your recitation of it, as He said: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification﴾.

Since the Prophet's (ﷺ) haste in seizing the revelation and his eagerness for it indicate his complete love for knowledge and his keenness for it, Allah commanded him to ask for an increase in knowledge, for knowledge is good, abundance of good is sought, and it comes from Allah. The way to it is diligence, longing for knowledge, asking Allah, seeking His help, and turning to Him in need at all times. ﴿And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge﴾.

From this noble verse is derived the etiquette of receiving knowledge: the listener should be patient and wait until the one dictating or the teacher has finished his speech, which is connected part to part. When he has finished, the listener should ask if he has a question. He should not hasten to ask or interrupt the speaker of knowledge, for that is a cause of deprivation. Likewise, the one being asked should listen carefully (yastamli) to the questioner's question and understand its intended meaning before answering, for that is a cause of reaching the correct answer.

{115} That is: We had already charged Adam, commanded him, and made a covenant with him that he would carry it out. He accepted it, submitted to it, complied, and resolved to fulfil it. Yet despite this, he forgot what he had been commanded, and his firm resolve gave way, so what befell him befell him, and he became a lesson for his descendants. Their natures became like the nature of Adam: he forgot, and his descendants forgot; he erred, and they erred; and they did not remain steadfast in the firm resolve, as they were. He hastened to repent of his sin, acknowledged it and confessed it, and so he was forgiven. "And whoever resembles his father has not wronged."

Then he mentioned the detail of what he had summarised, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verse 116–122:

{116} That is: when He had completed the creation of Adam with His own hand, taught him the names, favoured him and honoured him, He commanded the angels to prostrate to him, in honour, glorification and reverence. They hastened to prostrate, complying with the command. Among them was Iblis, who was arrogant toward the command of his Lord and refused to prostrate to Adam, and said: ﴿I am better than him. You created me from fire, and You created him from clay.﴾

{117 – 118} Then his intense enmity toward Adam and his wife became evident, since he was an enemy of Allah, and the envy that was the cause of the enmity appeared from him. So Allah warned Adam and his wife against him, and said: ﴿Let him not drive you both out of the Garden, so that you become miserable﴾ if you are expelled from it, for you have in it provision that is easy and complete comfort: ﴿Indeed, it is [granted] to you that you will not hunger therein or go naked, and that you will not thirst therein or be exposed to the sun﴾; that is, the sun will strike you with its heat. Thus He guaranteed him the continuance of food, drink, clothing and water, and the absence of fatigue and toil. But He forbade him from eating from a specific tree, saying: ﴿And do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers.﴾

{120} Satan never ceased to whisper to them and to make the eating of the tree appealing, saying: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾; that is, [the tree] whoever eats from it will remain forever in the Garden, and ﴿a kingdom that does not decay﴾; that is, it will not come to an end if you eat from it.

{121} He came to him in the form of a counsellor and was gentle with him in speech, so Adam was deceived by him, and they both ate from the tree. Then they were overcome with regret, their garments fell from them, their disobedience became manifest, and the private parts of each became visible to the other after they had been covered. They began to fasten upon themselves leaves from the trees of the Garden, so as to conceal themselves thereby, and they were seized with a shame that only Allah knows the extent of. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he erred.﴾ They hastened to repentance and turning back to Allah, and said:

{122} ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.﴾ Then his Lord chose him, selected him, and made repentance easy for him, so He accepted his repentance and guided him. He became, after repentance, better than he was before it. The plot of the enemy turned back against him and his scheming was nullified, so the blessing was completed upon him and upon his descendants, and it became obligatory upon them to uphold it, to acknowledge it, and to be on guard against this enemy who lies in wait for them and remains with them night and day. ﴿O Children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his soldiers, from where you cannot see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe.﴾

Ibn Sa'di's Commentary (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 20, verses 123–127:

{123} He, exalted is He, informs that He commanded Adam and Iblis to descend to the earth, and that they should take Satan as an enemy, so that they would take precaution against him, prepare their equipment against him, and fight him. He would send down Books and send Messengers to them, who would make clear to them the straight path that leads to Him and to His Paradise, and warn them of this manifest enemy. Whenever that guidance, which is the Books and the Messengers, comes to them, whoever follows it will follow what he was commanded and avoid what he was forbidden. He will not go astray in this world or in the Hereafter, nor will he be miserable in either of them. Rather, he has been guided to the straight path in this world and the Hereafter, and for him there is happiness and security in the Hereafter. In another verse He negated fear and grief from him, saying: ﴿So whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾. Following guidance means affirming the report and not opposing it with doubts, and carrying out the command by not opposing it with desire.

{124} ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾: that is, from My Book, by which all lofty matters are remembered, and he abandons it by turning away from it, or by something worse than that, by denying it and disbelieving in it. ﴿Indeed, for him is a constricted life﴾: that is, his recompense is that We make his livelihood narrow and hardship-laden, and this can be nothing other than punishment. The "constricted life" has been interpreted as the punishment of the grave, that his grave is constricted for him, he is confined in it, and he is punished as recompense for his turning away from the remembrance of his Lord. This is one of the verses indicating the punishment of the grave.
The second: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are extending their hands…﴾ [the verse].
The third: His saying: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment before the greater punishment﴾.
The fourth: His saying about the family of Pharaoh: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening…﴾ [the verse].
What led those among the early scholars who interpreted it as the punishment of the grave only, and restricted it to that, to do so—and Allah knows best—is the end of the verse, in which Allah mentions in it the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.
Some exegetes hold that the "constricted life" is general in the abode of this world, through the worries, griefs and pains that afflict one who turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, which is an immediate punishment; and in the intermediate abode (al-barzakh) and in the Hereafter, because the phrase "constricted life" is unrestricted and not specified. ﴿And We will gather him﴾: that is, this one who turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, blind﴾: in sight, according to the correct view, as Allah says: ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf﴾.

Commentary on verse 128: {Did it not guide them} — that is, to these deniers who turn away: that God has destroyed before them the earlier generations and successive nations, whose stories they know, whose tales they relate, and whose dwellings they see with their own eyes after them, such as the people of Hud, Salih, Lut and others. When they denied Our messengers and turned away from Our books, We struck them with a painful punishment. So what assures these people that what befell those will not befall them? {Are your disbelievers better than those, or do you have immunity in the Scriptures, or do they say, "We are a united force that will prevail"?} — No, none of this at all. These disbelievers are not better than those, so that punishment might be averted from them by their goodness. Rather, they are worse than them, because they disbelieved in the noblest of messengers and the best of books. They have no written immunity or covenant with God. They are not as they claim, that their numbers will benefit them and protect them; rather, they are far more humbled and contemptible than that. So the destruction of past generations for their sins is among the means of guidance, because it is among the signs that indicate the truth of the messages of the messengers who came to them and the falsehood of what they were upon. But not everyone benefits from the signs; only {people of understanding} benefit from them, that is, sound intellects, upright natures, and minds that restrain their possessors from what is not fitting.

This is a consolation and encouragement to the Messenger, to restrain him from hastening the destruction of those who deny and turn away, and [it shows] that their disbelief and denial are a sufficient cause for the punishment to descend upon them and to cling to them; because Allah has made punishments a consequence arising from sins and inseparable from them. These people have indeed committed the cause, but what has delayed it from them is the Word of your Lord, which includes granting them respite and postponement and setting a specified term. So the specified term and the execution of Allah's Word are what has deferred the punishment from them until its appointed time. Perhaps they will return to the command of Allah, and He will turn to them in forgiveness and lift the punishment from them, if the Word has not been fulfilled against them.

{130} Therefore Allah commanded His Messenger to be patient over their harm by speech, and commanded him to compensate for that and to seek help in it through glorifying his Lord, {with the praise of} his Lord, at these virtuous times: {before the rising of the sun and before its setting}, and at the extremities of the day, its beginning and its end; a general statement after a specific one, and the times and hours {of the night}, so that perhaps if you do that you will be content with what your Lord gives you of reward, both immediate and deferred, and so that your heart may be reassured and your eye comforted by worshipping your Lord, and you will be consoled by it regarding their harm; thus patience will then become easy for you.

This is a consolation and encouragement to the Messenger, to restrain him from hastening the destruction of those who deny and turn away, and [it shows] that their disbelief and denial are a sufficient cause for the punishment to descend upon them and to cling to them; because Allah has made punishments a consequence arising from sins and inseparable from them. {132} That is: urge your family to prayer, and rouse them to it, both obligatory and voluntary. Commanding a thing is a command to all that is necessary for it to be completed, so this is a command to teach them what makes the prayer valid, what invalidates it, and what perfects it. {And persevere in it} — that is, in the prayer, by establishing it with its limits, its pillars, [its etiquettes] and its humility (khushu'), for this is hard on the soul. Rather, one should compel the soul and strive against it to do so, and remain patient with it constantly. For when a servant establishes his prayer in the manner commanded, it is more protective and upright for the rest of his religion; and when he neglects it, the rest of his religion is more neglected. Then Allah, exalted is He, guaranteed His Messenger provision, and that his concern for it would not distract him from establishing his religion, so He said: {We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you}. That is: your provision is upon Us; We have undertaken it just as We have undertaken the provision of all creatures. How then would it be for one who stands by Our command and busies himself with remembering Us? Allah's provision is general, for the God-fearing and others alike; so one should be concerned with what brings everlasting happiness, which is taqwa (God-consciousness). Hence He said: {And the best outcome} — in this world and the Hereafter — {is for taqwa}, which is doing what is commanded and abstaining from what is forbidden. Whoever establishes it will have the outcome, as Allah, the Exalted, said: {And the best outcome is for the God-fearing}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 20, verses 133–135:

{133} Meaning: The deniers of the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" They meant the signs of suggestion (ayat al-iqtira'), like their saying: ﴿And they said, "We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palm trees and grapevines and cause rivers to gush forth within them in force, or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments, as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us in group."﴾ This is their obstinacy, defiance and wrongdoing. For they, and the Messenger, are mere human servants of Allah. It is not fitting for them to make suggestions according to their whims. Rather, the One who sends down signs and chooses from them what He wills, according to His wisdom, is Allah. Since their saying, ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾ implies that he had not brought them a sign attesting to his truthfulness or a proof of his right, and this is a lie and a fabrication, for he brought manifest miracles and overpowering signs, of which some suffice to achieve the purpose, He said: ﴿Has there not come to them [the clear evidence]﴾, if they are truthful in their saying and that they seek the truth through its proof, ﴿the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures﴾; that is, this great Qur'an, which confirms what is in the former scriptures of the Torah, the Gospel and the earlier books, agrees with them, reports what they reported, and its confirmation is also mentioned in them, and it gives good news of the Messenger through them. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and reminder for a people who believe.﴾ So the signs benefit the believers, and their faith and certainty increase through them; but as for those who turn away from them and oppose them, they do not believe in them and do not benefit from them. ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾

{134} The benefit of presenting them to the people and addressing them with them is that the proof of Allah may be established against them, and so that they will not say when punishment befalls them: ﴿Why did You not send to us a messenger so that we could follow Your signs before we are humiliated and disgraced?﴾ by punishment. So indeed My messenger has come to you with My signs and My proofs. If you are as you claim, then believe him.

{135} ﴿Say﴾: O Muhammad, addressing the deniers of you who say, "Wait for him, the misfortune of death." ﴿Say, "Each is waiting, so wait."﴾ You wait for me to die, and I wait for you to receive punishment. ﴿Say, "Do you wait for us except for one of the two good outcomes?"﴾ that is, victory or martyrdom. So we wait for Allah to strike you with a punishment from Him or by our hands. ﴿So wait; indeed, you will know who are the companions of the even path﴾; that is, the straight one, ﴿and who is rightly guided﴾ by following it, I or you. For its follower is the successful, rightly guided, saved and prosperous one, while whoever deviates from it is the losing, disappointed and punished one. It is known that the Messenger is in this state, and his enemies are contrary to it. And Allah knows best.

Since their saying, ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾ implies that he had not brought them a sign attesting to his truthfulness or a proof of his right, and this is a lie and a fabrication, for he brought manifest miracles and overpowering signs, of which some suffice to achieve the purpose, He said: ﴿Has there not come to them [the clear evidence]﴾, if they are truthful in their saying and that they seek the truth through its proof, ﴿the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures﴾; that is, this great Qur'an, which confirms what is in the former scriptures of the Torah, the Gospel and the earlier books, agrees with them, reports what they reported, and its confirmation is also mentioned in them, and it gives good news of the Messenger through them. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and reminder for a people who believe.﴾ So the signs benefit the believers, and their faith and certainty increase through them; but as for those who turn away from them and oppose them, they do not believe in them and do not benefit from them. ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾

{134} The benefit of presenting them to the people and addressing them with them is that the proof of Allah may be established against them, and so that they will not say when punishment befalls them: ﴿Why did You not send to us a messenger so that we could follow Your signs before we are humiliated and disgraced?﴾ by punishment. So indeed My messenger has come to you with My signs and My proofs. If you are as you claim, then believe him.

{135} ﴿Say﴾: O Muhammad, addressing the deniers of you who say, "Wait for him, the misfortune of death." ﴿Say, "Each is waiting, so wait."﴾ You wait for me to die, and I wait for you to receive punishment. ﴿Say, "Do you wait for us except for one of the two good outcomes?"﴾ that is, victory or martyrdom. For its follower is the successful, rightly guided, saved and prosperous one, while whoever deviates from it is the losing, disappointed and punished one. It is known that the Messenger is in this state, and his enemies are contrary to it. And Allah knows best.
